sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Every fullstack Java developer must be able to produce valid, semantic, accessible HTML and apply CSS layout confidently. Interviewers check this because poorly structured HTML breaks SEO and accessibility, and inability to use Flexbox or Grid is an immediate red flag in any frontend-touching role. Even if you spend 80% of your time on the backend, the frontend interview round will include at least two or three HTML/CSS questions.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **HTML = structure**: semantic tags describe *meaning*, not appearance.
- **CSS = style**: the cascade is just a priority chain — specificity wins, then source order.
- **Box model**: every element is a box; `box-sizing: border-box` means the size you set *includes* padding and border.
- **Flexbox = one axis**: use it for navbars, button groups, centering a single item.
- **Grid = two axes**: use it for page-level layouts and card grids.
- **Responsive = fluid first**: start with relative units (`%`, `rem`) and use `@media` only to override edge cases.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **html5-semantic-elements**: know `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>` and why they beat `<div>` for accessibility and SEO.
- **css-box-model**: be able to draw the four layers (content / padding / border / margin) and explain `box-sizing: border-box`.
- **css-flexbox**: drill `display:flex`, `justify-content`, `align-items`, `flex-wrap`, and what `flex: 1` means.
- **css-grid**: know `grid-template-columns`, `fr` unit, `gap`, `auto-fill` vs `auto-fit`.
- **responsive-design-media-queries**: understand mobile-first ordering and `min-width` breakpoints.
- **css-specificity-cascade**: calculate specificity for `#id .class element` and explain why `!important` is a last resort.
- **accessibility-basics**: know `alt`, `aria-label`, `role`, and why semantic HTML already helps screen readers.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"What is the difference between `<section>` and `<article>`?"* — `<article>` is self-contained and reusable (a blog post, a product card); `<section>` groups related content within a page.
- *"Explain the CSS box model."* — Content → padding → border → margin; `border-box` includes padding and border in the declared width.
- *"When would you choose Flexbox over Grid?"* — Flexbox for single-axis (navbar, row of buttons); Grid for two-dimensional layout (page skeleton, card grids).
- *"How do you center a div both horizontally and vertically?"* — `display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center` on the parent is the modern answer.
- *"What does `rem` mean and why use it over `px`?"* — `rem` is relative to the root font size, so scaling the root changes everything, which helps accessibility and responsive design.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"Semantic HTML tags like `<article>` and `<section>` give meaning to content beyond just visual presentation — search engines can index them better and screen readers use them to build a navigation structure for visually impaired users. When I structure a page I start with the semantic skeleton, then apply CSS using Flexbox for component-level layouts and Grid for the overall page layout, using `rem` units and `@media` min-width breakpoints so the design is mobile-first and scales cleanly on larger screens."*
